subject: Reserved pool: throughput windows & GPU shortlist (post-demo action items)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved pool: throughput windows & GPU shortlist (post-demo action items)

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the demo time today. Short recap + next steps from our side so we can get you a focused dedicated-capacity validation: 

What we heard (from the call):
- Target latency: you called out ~200ms p95 for simple completions and ~120ms p95 for streaming-style responses when possible.
- Concurrency & bursts: baseline around 1k concurrent users, peak bursts up to ~3k for product launch windows.
- Typical output sizes: ~30–60 tokens per response (median ~45).
- Streaming: ~70% of requests are streaming; the rest are short completions.

Before we schedule the benchmark run we need a couple clarifications so we size the reserved pool and pick the GPU shortlist properly: 
1) Confirm the p95 latency objective you want Redwood to validate against for the dedicated pool (200ms streaming? 120ms streaming? 95th vs 99th?).
2) Can you confirm steady-state QPS (or tokens/sec) vs expected peak burst duration (minutes)? Example: is the 3k concurrency burst expected to last <5 minutes or sustained for longer?
3) Any strict SLO on cold-start time (first token latency after model warmup)?
4) Do you expect end-to-end streaming with client-side aggregation or are you doing server-side aggregation? This affects batch sizing and KV cache behavior.

Proposed Redwood validation plan (high level):
- Run a half-day benchmark in our Dedicated validation environment with three configurations across GPU family + quantization to measure p50/p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec.
- Config matrix: H100 FP16 baseline, H100 q4_0, L40S q8_0 (cost vs latency tradeoffs).
- Reserved throughput candidates: 9k tokens/sec steady, 27k tokens/sec burst capacity; we'll tune batch windows to keep p95 under your target.
- Streaming test: simulate 70% streaming at median 45 tokens (token-per-sec profile will be in the attached spec).

Next steps I suggest: 
- Please answer the 4 clarifying items above.
- Confirm procurement contact for the PO and whether we can run the benchmark under a signed MSA/NDA (we can route DocuSign).
- If that looks good, we’ll lock a Wed/Thu half-day slot (proposal: Sep 2) and share the benchmark spec + data collection plan.

Attachments: benchmark-specs.xlsx (load pattern & prompt corpus), redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (reserved pool options).

Thanks — happy to be concise on any of the items above.

— Jordan

From: Aisha Gupta <aisha@clearpath.ai>

Subject: Re: Reserved pool: throughput windows & GPU shortlist (post-demo action items)

Jordan — great run this afternoon, appreciate the clear next steps. Answers inline: 

1) Latency objective: aim for p95 <= 200ms for non-streaming completions; for streaming the product team would prefer p95 <= 120ms but will accept 150ms if the quality/cost tradeoff is strong. If you can show p95 <=120ms on H100 that would be a big win.
2) Steady-state: we expect ~1k concurrent sessions sustained (these are active API sessions). Peak bursts to 3k concurrent are likely during launches but typically last 10–20 minutes. We plan 3–4 launches per quarter.
3) Cold-start: important — first token latency should be under 1s after warmup; we will accept longer for full model load (if you can warm a model quickly or keep a warm pool that works).
4) Streaming: client-side aggregation; we stream token-by-token to the browser.

Procurement: procurement@clearpath.ai is the correct contact (Ravi is the procurement lead). We have a standard vendor onboarding change — they’ll need the SSO integration checklist and SOC2 evidence.

GPU preference: we prefer H100 for latency-critical endpoints but are cost-conscious; we’d like to see an L40S quantized run for cost/throughput tradeoffs.

Confirm Sep 2 for a half-day benchmark — please send a calendar invite and the DocuSign PO link.

— Aisha
Aisha Gupta
CTO, ClearPath AI
aisha@clearpath.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-26T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool: throughput windows & GPU shortlist (post-demo action items)

Quick engineering read and recommended validation matrix — taking Aisha’s answers into account: 

Assumptions from Aisha: p95 targets (200ms non-streaming, 120–150ms streaming preferred), steady 1k concurrency, 3k bursts lasting ~10–20m, median 45 tokens per response, 70% streaming.

Recommended test matrix (we should include in benchmark-specs.xlsx):
- Config A (latency baseline): H100 FP16, no extra quantization; target p95 <= 120ms streaming.
- Config B (latency/cost sweet spot): H100 q4_0; measure p95 delta and tokens/sec.
- Config C (cost-forward): L40S q8_0; measure whether we can sustain 9k tokens/sec steady and 27k tokens/sec burst while staying under p95 <= 200ms for non-streaming.

Sizing guidance for reserved pool (initial candidates):
- Steady reserved throughput: 9,000 tokens/sec (covers 1k concurrency * ~9 tokens/sec average per session given median response sizes).
- Burst buffer (provisioned burstable capacity): +18,000 tokens/sec (so 27,000 total) to cover 3k concurrency spikes for ~15 minutes.
- Model warm pool: keep 10–15 hot replicas to keep first token <1s in our infra assumptions. We can reduce to 6–8 if customers accept slightly longer cold-starts.

Implementation notes for benchmark:
- Streaming load generator: emulate token-by-token client-side streaming; measure p50/p95/p99 for first token and full-response completion.
- Batch windows: we’ll try continuous batching with 5–10ms batching thresholds for streaming to minimize artificial latency.
- KV cache: for multi-turn sessions we’ll enable prefix caching; we’ll run a second pass with cold-starts only to capture worst-case.

Attachments I’ll reference in the run: benchmark-specs.xlsx (payloads & load profiles), gpu-compare-notes.md (short notes on kernel behavior and expected perf deltas).

If these numbers look sane I’ll prepare the test harness and we can sign the PO to get production-like reserved capacity allocated for the experiment.

— Marcus
